sentences.l2: 在竞争激烈的零售行业，货架绝非随意摆放，而是数据反复推敲的结果。
sentences.l1: In the fiercely competitive retail industry, shelves are by no means arranged casually, but are the result of repeated deliberation over data.

sentences.l2: 超市收集顾客的结账记录，通过购物篮分析找出哪些商品常被一起购买。
sentences.l1: Supermarkets collect customers' checkout records and, through basket analysis, find out which products are often bought together.

sentences.l2: 其核心是关联规则，即从大量交易中提炼出“买了甲的人往往也买乙”的规律。
sentences.l1: Its core is association rules, that is, extracting from a large number of transactions the pattern that "people who bought A often also buy B."

sentences.l2: 最著名的案例是“啤酒与尿布”：据说年轻父亲下班后为孩子买尿布，常顺手带走啤酒，于是商家把两者陈列得更近，销量随之上升。
sentences.l1: The most famous case is "beer and diapers": it is said that young fathers, after getting off work, buy diapers for their children and often take some beer along while they are at it, so merchants displayed the two closer together, and sales rose accordingly.

sentences.l2: 这个故事真实与否尚有争议，却生动说明了数据的价值。
sentences.l1: Whether this story is true is still disputed, but it vividly illustrates the value of data.

sentences.l2: 如今，商家依据类似的分析调整陈列：把牛奶放在卖场最里面，让顾客穿过整条通道；把面包和果酱相邻摆放，刺激连带消费。
sentences.l1: Nowadays, merchants adjust their displays based on similar analyses: they put milk at the very back of the store, making customers walk through the whole aisle; they place bread and jam next to each other, stimulating additional purchases.

sentences.l2: 看似平常的货架，背后其实隐藏着对消费心理的精准把握。
sentences.l1: Behind seemingly ordinary shelves actually lies a precise grasp of consumer psychology.
